subject: forensic-medicine
title: Tattooing, Blackening and Singeing: Estimating Range

steps.title: Three skin marks of close discharge
steps.tx: Close firearm discharge stamps three distinct marks. **Burning and singeing** come from flame and hot gas. **Blackening or smudging** is smoke deposit that spreads widely and wipes off with a wet cloth. **Tattooing, stippling or peppering** is unburnt or partly burnt powder driven into the skin, which cannot be wiped away. Singed hairs may melt at the tips and solidify into clubbed ends as they cool.
steps.say: Flame singes, smoke smudges and wipes off, but powder tattooing is embedded in skin and stays for the pathologist.

steps.tx: Close discharge leaves two wipe tests around an entry hole. **Blackening or smudging** is a wide smoke film that lifts away when a wet cloth is passed over the skin. Unburnt or partly burnt powder grains, by contrast, are driven into the epidermis as stippling and stay put. Flame and hot gas may also singe nearby hairs, whose melted tips cool into clubbed ends. Together these marks place the muzzle within close range.

steps.title: Contact wounds and the muzzle imprint
steps.tx: In a tight contact shot the muzzle seals against skin, so soiling stays minimal outside while gases blast into the wound and tear deeper tissues in a **contact firearm wound**. Gas expanding under the skin lifts it back against the muzzle rim and stamps a muzzle imprint, a copy or recoil abrasion. Blood, hair and cloth fibres may be sucked back into the barrel by the vacuum after discharge, the back spatter phenomenon.
steps.say: Tight contact hides soot outside, tears tissue inside, stamps the muzzle print and can suck blood back into the barrel.

nodes.label: Skin lifts against the muzzle rim

steps.title: Contact over bone splits the wound
steps.tx: Where thick bone lies just under skin, as on the skull, contact discharge blows the wound open into **cruciate or stellate tears** because trapped gas has nowhere to expand. Margins split with subsidiary linear tears and the skull shows a large irregular hole with fissured fractures, burning and blackening in its margins. On the abdomen, by contrast, gas entering the peritoneal cavity can push coils of small intestine out through the entry wound.
steps.say: Contact over skull bursts the entry into a star, while contact over belly can blow bowel out of the hole.

steps.title: Close range up to thirty centimetres
steps.tx: Within about thirty centimetres, the **close range wound** shows all three marks together: tissues are singed by flame, blackened by smoke and tattooed by powder. If the powder is smokeless the deposit may look greyish or white instead of black. A circular burnt area means the gun fired at a right angle; an oval area means an angled shot, with the wound sitting nearer the end from which the shot travelled.
steps.say: Inside thirty centimetres expect singeing, smudge and stipple together, round for square shots and oval for angled ones.

steps.title: Thirty centimetres to one metre
steps.tx: From thirty centimetres to one metre the flame and smoke effects fade, but tattooing persists and the tissues along the track turn cherry red from carbon monoxide in the gases, the **cherry red wound track** sign. Margins grow irregular and scalloped into the so called rat hole, with annular bruising from gas entry. Wads and plastic cups are found deep inside, and a plastic cup opening between thirty and sixty centimetres can print a Maltese cross abrasion.
steps.say: Past thirty centimetres the stipple and cherry red track remain, the rim turns rat hole, and wads hide deep inside.

steps.title: Short and intermediate shotgun ranges
steps.tx: Shotgun pattern grows with distance in a predictable ladder of **shotgun range patterns**. Between one and two metres the shot mass still enters as one round hole of four to five centimetres for every gauge and choke. From two metres the mass begins to spread and separate pellet holes appear around a shrinking centre. At three metres the central hole is ringed by satellites across eight to ten centimetres.
steps.say: One solid hole to two metres, satellites by three metres: the pellet pattern is a measuring tape on the skin.

steps.tx: At three metres a shotgun charge no longer punches one clean hole. **Shotgun range patterns** show a shrinking central defect ringed by separate satellite pellet holes spread across eight to ten centimetres. From one metre to two the whole shot mass still enters as a single round wound of four to five centimetres, whatever the gauge and choke. From two metres onward the mass starts to separate, so satellite holes first appear around a narrowing centre.

steps.title: Distant range and choke effects
steps.tx: Beyond four metres every pellet travels alone in the **distant shotgun wound**, each making its own small opening with an abrasion rim. Spread from a fully choked barrel widens steadily at ten, fifteen and twenty metres, which lets the examiner work backward to distance. A sawn off barrel starts spreading as early as one metre, while a full choke gun may hold together to four metres, so barrel length must be known.
steps.say: Past four metres pellets fly solo, and the same spread means a shorter range from a sawn off than a choked barrel.

steps.title: Rifle and pistol range markers
steps.tx: Rifled weapons leave tighter limits: flame reaches 15 to 20 centimetres, smoke vanishes beyond thirty centimetres and unburnt grains are not found past one metre in **rifle discharge range signs**. The rifle entry is usually smaller than the bullet, like a lead pencil hole, sometimes without an abrasion collar, ringed by one to two millimetre micro tears and a reddish zone that browns on drying. Clothing may hold the only range evidence.
steps.say: Rifle flame stops near twenty centimetres and powder near a metre, so the shirt may carry more range evidence than skin.

steps.title: Traps that falsify range estimation
steps.tx: Several devices and conditions corrupt the pattern. **Silencers, muzzle brakes and flash hiders** cut smoke and powder or throw them in odd directions, imitating long range. A shortened barrel deforms bullets. Clothing layers can filter out every discharge product except the bullet itself, while smoke trapped between skin and cloth blackens inner garment surfaces even in contact shots. Infrared photography can still reveal blackening and tattooing on dark skin and fabric.
steps.say: Silencers, sawn barrels and layered clothing all fake a longer range, so reconstruct the whole firing setup before opining.
